title: Tool-call bounded stream fragment rewrite and retry spec
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem statement:
When model responses are streamed in the middle of a tool/function call, truncation or transport retries can leave clients with malformed structured JSON or orphaned tool boundaries. Current approaches either force the client to accept invalid JSON or rely on heuristics that are brittle across SDKs and proxies. This ticket defines a pragmatic, backward-compatible server+client protocol to make streaming structured outputs (including tool/function call envelopes) resumable and reparable without breaking older clients. It also defines a compatibility shim so older SDKs can opt-in to fallbacks.
background_and_motivation: Recent incidents: two customer apps crashed when a tool call payload was truncated mid-array and the client JSON parser threw. We need a deterministic, low-latency way to resume or repair streams that: 1) preserves tool-call boundaries, 2) avoids large buffering on-hosted tier, and 3) provides clear migration steps for SDKs and proxies.
proposal_summary: Introduce a compact fragment header per stream chunk (ASCII header line) carrying: fragment_id, seq_no, final_flag (F/..), crc32, and optional resume_token. Server emits header+payload lines. Clients parse header tolerant-mode. On truncation or reconnect, client sends last_ack_seq + resume_token to request remaining fragments. For older clients we detect absence of header and use a compatible escape wrapper: server will emit an extra final sentinel chunk containing a minimal repair manifest that older clients will ignore but can be used by newer SDKs to reconstruct the final JSON. The protocol works with function/tool calls by including an envelope field 'toolBoundary' in the header and ensuring idempotency keys on retries.
detailed_spec:
Chunk format (ASCII-first line + binary payload): <FRAG-HDR>
<payload bytes>
-- where FRAG-HDR = 'RWF/1 ' fragment_id ' ' seq '/' final ' ' crc32 [' ' resume_token]
Example header: 'RWF/1 abc123 7/F 1a2b3c4d rt:ZGFy' followed by chunk payload. Sequence numbers increase monotonically for a single response stream.

final flag values: 'F' = final chunk for the response, '.' = non-final. If a stream ends mid-json, the final chunk must contain either the remaining bytes that complete the JSON or a repair manifest (see below).

resume_token: opaque short token (base62) allowing server to map to transient buffer state. Token TTL = 60s by default for hosted API, configurable per-customer for Dedicated/Private. Token makes resumptions cheap without full re-rendering.
CRC32 covers only the payload bytes for quick corruption detection. If CRC mismatch occurs on client receive, client requests resend from last good seq.

Tool/function envelope: header includes optional 'TB=' field indicating toolBoundary id and 'IK=' idempotency_key. On resume, server guarantees at-least-once delivery of remaining fragments for that toolBoundary but will not re-execute external tool actions; idempotency_key must be honored by any platform side actions.

Repair manifest (for truncated finalization): small JSON patch-like structure encoded as base64 in the final fragment when the server can't stream the final bytes immediately. Manifest items: expected_tail_length, minimal_patch_ops, escape_map hints. New SDKs use manifest+cached fragments to reconstruct; older SDKs will see the final bytes omitted but can still surface partial text (compat mode).

Backwards compatibility: if client does not advertise support (via header 'X-Redwood-Stream-V' in request), server falls back to existing streaming behavior but will emit a final 'legacy-repair' sentinel line that older clients ignore, and new clients can use when available. This avoids breaking proxies that strip unknown headers.

Server-side memory bounds: do not keep full response longer than 'buffer_window' (default 60s). If a client resumes after token expiry, server will redirect client to issue a new request using idempotency key to regenerate response or fall back to canonical non-streamed response (error code 409 with 'resume_expired' reason).

Security: resume_token is ephemeral and tied to request context; treat as bearer token with short TTL. Ensure tokens are not leaked to logs. Mark security_review_required=true on the ticket and include KMS integration for Private deployments where required.

Observability: emit metrics stream_resume_attempts, stream_resume_success_rate, stream_crc_errors, stream_manifest_generated, stream_resume_latency, and tools_replay_attempts. Attach trace id to each fragment header when tracing is enabled.

SDK behavior (new clients): parse FRAG-HDR, validate crc, append payload, ack by sending last_seq in a resume handshake on reconnect, support 'tolerant parse' mode that attempts to salvage partial JSON using the repair manifest. SDK exposes a high-level event API: onFragment, onRepairCandidate, onFinalizedObject, onToolBoundary(toolId, payload).

SDK fallback (older clients): unchanged behavior; they will receive payload bytes as before. If legacy-repair sentinel exists, they ignore it. Document migration guide and bump supported SDK versions to pick up header parsing.

Proxy behavior: proxies that buffer entire responses can remove headers; guidance: transparently pass header lines as ASCII preface. For gateways that terminate HTTP/2 streams, we provide a shim that converts FRAG-HDR prefaces into HTTP trailers for compatibility where needed.
Admin console and console replay: add a 'stream fragments' view in the Console that shows per-fragment header metadata, repair manifests, and resume_attempt logs for troubleshooting.

Failure modes: if resume fails repeatedly, provide a 'best-effort' aggregated truncation event which contains the last N bytes and the manifest; Console will surface this as a 'partial-structured-output' incident with customer-visible reason.

Rollout strategy: staged feature flag default-off for hosted API. Turn on for internal Canary customers first, then opt-in customers, then gradual default enablement after 6 weeks of telemetry. Dedicated/Private customers can opt-in on their upgrade path.

Migration: document SDK changes and add an agent in the SDKs to preserve backwards compatibility for proxies that drop the header. Provide a small polyfill that consumes sentinel manifest from legacy streams to attempt best-effort repair on older runtimes.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits FRAG-HDR preface for streamed responses when feature-flag enabled.
SDK unit tests validate CRC mismatches trigger resend request and successful repair with manifest.
Integration test: simulated truncated final chunk + resume within TTL results in a fully parseable JSON object and preserved tool/function call boundary.
Console surfaces fragment metadata and replay log for at least 30 days in internal canary and admin mode.
Fallback: legacy clients without 'X-Redwood-Stream-V' header continue to receive streaming text and do not error out.
Security review sign-off completed and resume_token secrets are not logged in plaintext in any service logs.
Metrics: stream_resume_success_rate >= 95% in canary after 2 weeks, stream_crc_errors below 0.1% of stream bytes transferred.
Rolling upgrade plan documented and validated with one Dedicated customer in staging.
implementation_notes: Server: extend response writer to prefix each chunk with ASCII preface.
Server: implement short-lived resume_token store with TTL eviction (redis/small in-memory cache).
Server: CRC32 compute path must be zero-copy on fast path and not add >0.5ms to p99 token latency.
SDKs: add parser module 'streamFragments' in js/py/go SDKs. Provide permissive parser for partial JSON with repair manifest application. Add unit tests with randomized truncation fuzzing.

Console: new panel to show 'fragment timeline' tied to trace id. Store a compact index rather than full payload for privacy; provide 'download payload' option for troubleshooting with access controls.
PRs: backend PRs should reference GH# redwood-inference/runtime PRs (placeholder) and include benchmark numbers for p50/p95 latency before and after change.
Backwards compatibility checklist: confirm header lines pass through AWS ALB/NLB, GCP load balancers and common proxies used by customers. Add tests that run through our e2e gateway layer.
Edge cases: extremely small token budgets (mobile clients) should be able to opt-out via query param 'stream_fragments=off' to avoid resume token generation.
test_plan: Unit tests for header serialization/deserialization across SDKs.
Fuzz tests: truncated stream + random byte corruption + resume token expiry scenarios.
Integration: simulated network flaps (client disconnects/reconnects) with sequence drifts and out-of-order chunk arrival.
Canary: enable for 5 internal services and monitor resume metrics + error budgets for 2 weeks.
Compatibility tests: replay through common proxies (nginx, istio, envoy) and ensure header lines survive.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement server + SDK support behind feature flag (internal-only).
2) Smoke test in internal canary namespace for 3 days.
3) Open opt-in for 10 selected customers and monitor metrics.
4) After 6 weeks and postmortem review, flip feature flag wider in waves by region.
5) Announce migration guide and SDK updates to customers and publish Console tooling docs.
